title: Graceful shutdown with signal handling and request draining
description: Adds support for SIGINT/SIGTERM handling so the server can stop accepting new connections, wait for in‑flight requests to finish, then close resources cleanly. This prevents abrupt termination, improves reliability in container orchestration and reduces the risk of corrupted responses.
testCases: Simulate SIGTERM during an active request and verify the server stops accepting new connections but completes the ongoing request before exiting
Send multiple concurrent requests, trigger SIGINT, and ensure all responses are received and the process exits with code 0
acceptance: When the process receives SIGINT or SIGTERM, the server stops accepting new connections, waits up to 30 seconds for all active requests to finish, then closes the HTTP server and exits with code 0. No new connections are accepted after the signal, and all pending responses are delivered correctly.
reason: Production deployments (Kubernetes, Docker, PM2) rely on graceful shutdown to avoid dropped requests and ensure clean resource cleanup. Implementing this feature enhances stability, aligns with the framework's zero‑dependency, production‑ready ethos, and addresses a common operational pain point.
